title: Book 1 — Clio, Chapter 3
paragraphs: In the next generation, the Persians say, Alexander, the son of Priam, heard of these events and wanted to get a wife for himself out of Hellas by force, certain that he would never be required to give satisfaction, since the Hellenes had given none themselves. So he carried off Helen. The Hellenes decided first to send messengers demanding her back along with compensation for the abduction. When they pressed this demand, the Trojans threw the abduction of Medea back at them, pointing out that the Hellenes were now demanding from others what they themselves had refused to give, and had not surrendered the woman when she was demanded of them.
